scope: Optimistic cost diagnostic for existing v79 eight-engine profiler only, not a universal lower bound. A racing method that still initializes every width cannot remove more than all measured generation time if non-generation overhead is unchanged.
conclusion: Even eliminating ALL warmup and timed generation would save less than 10 percent total profiling time. Do not launch naive successive elimination as a plausible 10 percent total-cost improvement under this engine lifecycle.
limitations: Counterfactual arithmetic, not measured racing performance.
Changing number of initialized widths or sharing an engine invalidates this bound.
A prior shortlist must compete against zero-profile transfer and equal-cost shortlist baselines.
This is profiling cost only, not steady-state inference throughput.
